### 2. Role Recommendations & Decision Tradeoffs

#### Role 1: Travel-Heavy General User
* **Best Fit: MacBook Air 13-inch (M5, 16 GB RAM, 512 GB SSD) — £1,299**
  * *Why:* Extremely lightweight (1.24 kg / 2.7 lbs), fanless and silent, up to 18 hours battery life, 500-nit Liquid Retina display, and native dual external display support.
  * *Tradeoffs:* Lacks an internal fan (throttles slightly under prolonged heavy compute) and has only two Thunderbolt ports without built-in HDMI or SD card reader.
* **Fallback Options:**
  * *MacBook Air 15-inch (M5, £1,499):* Larger display canvas and 6-speaker audio, but heavier (1.51 kg) and bulkier on plane/train tray tables.
  * *MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, £699):* Substantially lower cost, but limited to lighter workloads, smaller display, and 1 external screen.

#### Role 2: Software Developer
* **Best Fit: MacBook Pro 14-inch (M5 Pro, 24 GB RAM, 1 TB SSD, Space Black) — £2,499**
  * *Why:* The 15-core CPU (5 super + 10 performance cores) with active cooling handles sustained builds and parallel test suites without thermal throttling; 24 GB unified memory accommodates Docker, local VMs, and multiple IDEs; three Thunderbolt 5 (120 Gb/s) ports allow connecting up to three 6K external monitors directly; 120Hz ProMotion Liquid Retina XDR screen.
  * *Tradeoffs:* Slightly heavier (1.6 kg) and more expensive than base models; power adapter is sold separately on current configurations.
* **Fallback Options:**
  * *Mac mini M5 Pro (£1,699) or M6 (£899):* Incredible desk-bound price-to-performance, but entirely lacks portability.
  * *MacBook Pro 14-inch M5 Base (£1,999):* Retains the XDR chassis and fan, but is limited to 16 GB base RAM and 2 external displays over Thunderbolt 4.

#### Role 3: Photo/Video Creator
* **Best Fit: Mac Studio (M5 Max, 36 GB RAM, 512 GB SSD) — £2,499**
  * *Why:* Workstation-class performance with 460 GB/s memory bandwidth, dual video encode engines, dual ProRes engines, 32-core GPU, and an advanced dual centrifugal cooling system designed for non-stop rendering without thermal drop-offs. Includes front-facing SDXC and USB-C ports, four rear Thunderbolt 5 ports, 10Gb Ethernet, and drive support for up to five external displays.
  * *Tradeoffs:* Headless desktop; requires dedicated external display, keyboard, and mouse.
* **Fallback Options:**
  * *MacBook Pro 16-inch M5 Pro (£2,999):* Offers mobile editing flexibility with a built-in 16.2" reference-grade XDR screen, but starts at a higher price and has lower memory bandwidth (approx. 273 GB/s vs 460 GB/s on Studio).
  * *iMac 24-inch M4 (£1,699):* Includes a sharp 4.5K screen and all peripherals in the box, but has a smaller 24-inch panel, consumer-tier M4 chip, and max 16–32 GB memory.
